# Draftera

> Draftera is the AI operations practice of Ken Hopkins, a former nonprofit executive director. It helps nonprofits and social enterprises use AI responsibly, with practical workflows, clear safeguards and services built on Draftera Foundations, a framework for using AI in nonprofits and social enterprises. Ken builds practical AI workflows alongside each organization's team, trains the staff who will use them and agrees clear guardrails with the organization. Based in Newfoundland and Labrador, working with nonprofits across Canada.

Draftera works with nonprofits, charities, social enterprises and associations, typically with annual revenue between about $1 million and $20 million. All prices are in Canadian dollars, plus applicable taxes, and depend on the size and needs of the organization. Any new AI tool licences are paid directly by the client organization. Every engagement starts with a free 30-minute conversation and, if working together makes sense, a written proposal with a fixed price before any work begins.

## The framework

- [Draftera Foundations](https://draftera.ca/foundations.html) A framework for using AI in nonprofits and social enterprises, version 0.1 (November 2026), reviewed annually. Four pieces concern governing AI (leadership and policy, data and privacy, human oversight, and transparency and trust) and two concern using it (people and skills, and value and measurement). An inventory and annual review keeps every piece current. It draws on the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, the OECD AI Principles and Canadian standards and guidance, including CAN/DGSI 101 and DGSI 135; a detailed mapping to CAN/DGSI 101 and DGSI 135 is in progress. Draftera prepares organizations for independent verification against CAN/DGSI 101, which is carried out by the Digital Governance Council. Draftera does not certify organizations and is independent of the Council. The framework is practical guidance, not legal advice.

## Services

- [Introductory Conversation](https://draftera.ca/conversation.html) A free 30-minute Google Meet call to discuss a recurring task, an operational challenge or an information session on AI for the organization's board or staff, explore what would help most and identify a practical next step. Every call leaves the organization with at least one practical idea, whether or not it goes on to work with Draftera.
- [AI policy](https://draftera.ca/services.html#ai-policy) From $1,500. A board-approved AI policy and a one-page plain-language guide for staff, with wording for the board minutes that record the approval.
- [Training](https://draftera.ca/services.html#training) From $950 per session. Information sessions and workshops for a board, leadership team or staff, each a tailored 90-minute session with a planning call, a handout and an attendance record. Networks and associations can book one session for several organizations.
- [Data and privacy review](https://draftera.ca/services.html#data-privacy-review) From $1,250. A list of the AI tools in use and the information that goes into them, rules on what stays out, and recommendations on tool settings. Practical guidance, not legal advice.
- [Workflow Build](https://draftera.ca/workflow-build.html) From $2,500 for one workflow, from $4,000 for two. A practical AI workflow for a real task, built with staff over two to three weeks, with a named person who checks the output, a short how-to, staff training, guardrails and a final report.
- [Transparency statement](https://draftera.ca/services.html#transparency-statement) From $350, as an add-on to any other service. A short public statement on how the organization uses AI.
- [Full Foundations](https://draftera.ca/services.html#full-foundations) From $6,500. Every piece of the framework, delivered in order, ending with a readiness summary against Canada's national standard for AI in small and medium organizations and including the first Foundations Check-up. Payment can be spread over stages or across two budget years.
- [Foundations Check-up](https://draftera.ca/services.html#foundations-check-up) From $1,500 per year. A yearly review that keeps every piece of the framework current.
- [Draftera Embedded AI Partnership](https://draftera.ca/partnership.html) An ongoing partner for AI and operations, covering implementation, adoption, maintenance, operational advice and reporting, with a quarterly impact report for leadership and the board. Core is $2,500 a month for one active priority at a time, and Plus is $4,500 a month for up to two active priorities at once. Both have a three-month minimum and then run month to month, and an organization can switch between them with 30 days' notice.

Operational work beyond AI, such as improving a process, implementing a change, reviewing roles and structure or supporting a stretched leadership team, can be one of the monthly Partnership priorities or a separate fixed-fee project.

## For partners

- [For partners](https://draftera.ca/partners.html) Draftera works with networks, associations, funders and sector bodies, from training sessions for members and grantees to group delivery of the full framework for a cohort. Partner work is scoped to fit and has no set price.

## How the work is done

- Client, donor and staff personal information never goes into outside AI tools without the organization's written agreement.
- Every workflow has a named person who checks what it produces, and staff remain responsible for the work.
- Draftera is tool-neutral and builds on tools the organization already has wherever possible, such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace or an existing AI subscription.
- Results are reported plainly, including when a workflow falls short.

## About Ken Hopkins

- [About Ken](https://draftera.ca/about.html) Ken Hopkins has more than two decades of experience leading organizations through growth and change. He spent six years (2013 to 2019) as Executive Director of the School Lunch Association in Newfoundland and Labrador, where revenue tripled and the program expanded to 34 school locations, serving over 1 million meals a year with a team of over 80 people. He also brings operational leadership experience from a large Canadian university, and for more than two years he has been building practical AI workflows with privacy safeguards, clear responsibilities and human review. He developed Draftera Foundations. He holds an MBA (Employee Relations) from the University of Leicester, a Master's Certificate in Project Management and a Certificate in Not-for-Profit Governance from Rotman, and is a Qualified Mediator.
